0.0.n: Refers to developing a character for a performance.

0.1.n: Marks 役作り as the description being considered in という.

0.2.n: いう literally means to say, but here helps introduce a description.

0.3.n: Introduces the description the speaker will replace with a more accurate one.

0.4.n: Adds contrast to より; というよりは means rather than describing it that way.

1.1.n: This first 私 is the person who wanted to become someone.

1.2.n: Marks the first 私 as the subject of なりたかった.

1.3.n: なる becomes なりたい for wanting to become, then なりたかった for past desire.

1.4.n: This second 私 is described by 私がなりたかった: the self the speaker wanted to become.

1.6.n: Casual version of という, linking the quoted phrase to 言葉.

1.7.n: Refers to the entire quoted phrase, not just one word.

1.8.n: Limits what the speaker kept in mind to those particular words.

1.9.n: Marks 言葉だけ as what the speaker put into their head.

1.10.n: 頭 literally means head; 頭に入れる means to keep something in mind.

1.11.n: Marks 頭 as the destination in the expression 頭に入れる.

1.12.n: 入れて links to やってました, a conversational shortening of やっていました describing what the speaker was doing.

2.0.n: First character of the name 灯花; the subtitle splits this name into two pieces.

2.1.n: Second character of the name 灯花, addressing the person directly.

2.3.n: The plain form 泣く combines with な to tell someone not to cry.

2.4.n: This is prohibitive な plus emphatic って, not a form of なる.

2.6.n: The person whose side is meant is understood from context.

2.7.n: Marks そば as the location where the speaker is present.

2.8.n: いる expresses the presence of a living being; the speaker is the unstated subject.

2.9.n: Gives the reassuring reason for asking Tohka not to cry.

3.0.n: With the negative wish, this naturally conveys not wanting to lose any of it.

3.2.n: This character starts 失くす; it is not a separate word here.

3.3.n: Completes 失くしたくない, the negative desire form of 失くす; it is not from くい.

3.4.n: Softens the statement into a personal feeling or wish, unlike the prohibitive な in 泣くな.

0.lit: Rather than calling it preparing for a role…
0.tip: というよりは introduces a more accurate description, which comes next.

1.lit: Only the words called “the me I wanted to become” into my head putting, I was doing it.
1.tip: 頭に入れる literally says put into your head, but means keep in mind here.

2.lit: Tohka, don't cry, I'm telling you. Because I'm by your side.
2.tip: 泣くな uses a plain verb plus な to say don't; って adds conversational emphasis.

3.lit: All of it, I don't want to lose, I feel.
3.tip: 失くしたくない means don't want to lose; final な makes the wish sound reflective.
